title: Unicellular and Multicellular Modes of Selection Impose Distinct Constraints on Cellular Phenotype Evolution: simulation code
description:
Simulation code accompanying Kim & Pennell, Unicellular and Multicellular Modes of Selection Impose Distinct Constraints on Cellular Phenotype Evolution.

A genome is a binary matrix mapping loci onto gene expression programs. For each task it deploys the non-negative program combination that best approximates that task's optimum. During each selective epoch m of the T task-specific phenotypes contribute jointly to fitness: m = 1 is sequential selection, m = T simultaneous, and intermediate m interpolates. The repository contains the SSWM engine, the run driver, and one script per manuscript figure.
